marker: # unit_length, ref_size and ref_repeats are the published values that the MLVAbank identifier in
# the label column encodes as NAME_<unit>bp_<size>bp_<n>u, taken from the source table of the
# bundled scheme bacillus_mlva31_mlvabank, which holds the 31 locus composite panel. The label
# therefore carries the MLVAbank name of the locus, which for the seven loci this panel adds is
# vntrNN rather than BaVNTRNN. No number in this table is derived.
# ref_size is also the product length measured in the Ames Ancestor assembly GCA_000008445.1 by
# in silico PCR with these primers, outer primer edge to outer primer edge. All fifteen agree
# with the identifier, every locus gives exactly one product, all are searchable at word size 11
# and none needs the rescue pass. Each product lies on the replicon the publication states: the
# eleven chromosomal loci on AE017334.2, pXO1-aat on pXO1 (AE017336.2) and BaVNTR16, BaVNTR17
# and pXO2-at on pXO2 (AE017335.3).
# BaVNTR32 is the one locus whose identifier does not describe this amplicon. It is the locus
# MLVAbank calls bams01, alias vntr32, and the two panels amplify it with different primer pairs,
# 485 bp there against 577 bp here, so the unit length and the copy number are taken from the
# identifier but ref_size is the product these primers give. The 21 bp unit it publishes confirms
# the unit derived from the reference for this locus, whose motif Van Ert et al. print only as
# Complex.
# The publication's locations are coordinates in the A2012 numbering (NC_003995 for the
# chromosome, NC_003980 for pXO1, NC_003981 for pXO2), not in Ames Ancestor, so they were
# compared by span length. All eight older loci reproduce their published span exactly.
# A non-genomic base in the new reverse primers. Each of the seven reverse primers this panel
# adds begins with a 5' G that the genome does not carry; six of them therefore report one primer
# mismatch, and in BaVNTR19 the G happens to match. The primers are kept as published, because a
# real reaction with them yields a product one base longer than the genomic span, and the
# published reference sizes already include that base. Taking it into account, six of the seven
# agree with the published span: BaVNTR12, BaVNTR35, BaVNTR16 and BaVNTR17 match it when the
# extra base is excluded (114, 114, 272, 385 bp), and BaVNTR23 and BaVNTR32 match it when the
# extra base is included, so the publication appears not to be consistent about whether the base
# is counted. BaVNTR19 is the exception: its published span is 124 bp, against 96 bp measured
# here. That one is a mistake in the publication rather than a strain difference, because the
# MLVAbank identifier for the same locus also gives 96 bp.
# patterns are kept only for the six loci whose published copy number equals the number of times
# the published motif occurs in the reference, so the tandem array cross-check is active on those
# six and skipped on the rest, where it would contradict the published number. The motifs are the
# published ones; BaVNTR32, vrrB1, vrrB2, vrrC1 and vrrC2 have no motif in the table, which
# prints them as Complex or, for vrrB1, as a 9 bp degenerate repeat. The two loci left without a
# pattern although their motif is known are pXO2-at, whose array holds ten TA units where the
# panel numbers the reference 9, and BaVNTR16, whose array holds 20 published units of ACATTTAC
# of which only four are perfect copies. An allele in this panel is therefore not always a
# literal count of whole units in the reference.
# vrrB1 and vrrB2 hold 20 and 13 units of 9 bp in a 229 and a 153 bp product, which leaves 49 and
# 36 bp outside the array, less than their two primers occupy, so for these two loci the primers
# lie inside the repeat array; the allele formula needs only the size and the copy number to be
# consistent, which they are. vrrB1 with vrrB2 and vrrC1 with vrrC2 are adjacent paralogues whose
# amplicons overlap by 27 and 36 bp, so a rearrangement there can move both members of a pair.
